title: Linux Networking
subtitle: Kernel plumbing from NIC to services, mapped to OSI L1 to L4

boxes.label: Uplink NIC
boxes.says: The NIC carries traffic to the wire.
boxes.detail: The physical interface sends translated packets out. Replies return through conntrack.

boxes.label: Namespace
boxes.detail: Each owns interfaces, routes and firewall rules. Containers live inside one.

boxes.label: veth pair
boxes.says: A veth pair is a cable.
boxes.detail: Frames entering one end exit the other. One end sits in the namespace.

boxes.label: Bridge
boxes.detail: Host-side veth ends attach to a bridge that learns MAC addresses.

boxes.label: Routing
boxes.detail: The kernel matches the longest prefix; the default route covers the rest.

boxes.label: ip_forward
boxes.says: ip_forward makes a host a router.
boxes.detail: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 lets packets cross interfaces. Without it, transit traffic is dropped.

boxes.label: NAT
boxes.detail: MASQUERADE rewrites private sources; conntrack maps replies. Alternative: nftables.

boxes.label: VRRP
boxes.detail: keepalived elects a master by priority. The backup takes over in seconds.

boxes.label: sshd
boxes.detail: PasswordAuthentication no, PermitRootLogin no, AllowUsers. Test with sshd -t.

boxes.label: dnsmasq
boxes.detail: Static records, forwarders and a cache on port 53.

boxes.label: HAProxy
boxes.detail: Binds the VIP that keepalived moves. Alternatives: NGINX, Envoy, cloud load balancers.

steps.title: Isolate
steps.text: A namespace gives the process its own stack.

steps.title: Switch
steps.text: veth ends attach to a bridge that learns MACs.

steps.title: Route and forward
steps.text: ip_forward lets the kernel route between subnets.

steps.title: Translate
steps.text: MASQUERADE rewrites sources; conntrack returns replies.

steps.title: Float and serve
steps.text: VRRP moves the VIP; sshd and dnsmasq answer on it.

declarations: A veth pair is a cable.

run.cmd: ip netns exec a1 ip route get 10.0.2.11
